reportedTitle: Use of password hash with insufficient computational effort

priorMappedLocation.expression: helperDigest of canonical helper request body

independentTrace: src/runtime/workspace-index.ts:26-42 validates one to32 explicit unique relative selected paths, with Git-stage file metadata checked separately.
src/runtime/workspace-witness.ts:88-94 enters the Git stage/unstage acknowledgement branch; line93 extracts only file path strings or the unstage paths array.
At line94, SHA256 hashes canonical(paths) and compares the result to row.pathsDigest together with selectedCount. This binds acknowledgement to the same ordered selection, not to a login/password.
deploy/workspace_index.py:102 extracts that same selected path list and line202 reports digest(selected) and its length.
src/gateway/receipt-result.ts:112-117 validates and projects pathsDigest/selectedCount; it does not carry the original selected path list into the retained result.

tests/runtime/workspace-witness.test.ts:161-170 checks mismatched count and reversed-order digest are rejected, and exact successful projection does not retain the selected path names. This existing test was read but not rerun.
securityInterpretation: The digest is an identity/integrity comparison for a Git selection. It is not password storage or a promise to make low-entropy file names unguessable. SHA256 computational cost is appropriate to this purpose; replacing it with password hashing is not justified by this alert.
limitations: Current alert location was supplied by the parent live UI inspection; this report independently inspects the exact current sink and its source/producer/consumer rather than relying only on an unchanged whole-file hash.
This is a correction for existing alert11, separate from the three newly reported alerts13-15.
